messages:
alex: Hey @people-ops — quick question: I enrolled with pre-tax 401(k) last month. Can I switch my deferral to Roth 401(k) mid-year? Also hearing there’s a vendor migration in July — will that freeze contribution or investment elections? Thanks!

anya: Short answer: yes, you can change your deferral election mid-year.
You just need to submit the change in the benefits portal before the payroll cutoff for the pay period you want it to take effect.
Also heads-up: we have a plan migration scheduled in July that will pause changes for a brief window.

marcus: Payroll note: cutoff for deferral/election changes is 5 business days before the pay date (EOY/bonus payrolls may have different rules). Example: if paydate = 2026-07-31 then cutoff = 2026-07-24 (or earlier if holiday/weekend).
We can’t promise changes submitted during the migration freeze will be processed until after cutover.

anya: To add detail: Roth vs pre-tax only affects how contributions are taxed now. Employer match rules are set by the plan document (see below) and are usually contributed to a traditional account. In-plan Roth conversions (if you do one) are a taxable event — coordinate with finance.

priya: Finance check-in: in-plan Roth conversions are reported as taxable income on your W-2. We do not automatically withhold additional tax for the conversion amount, so you may want to adjust your W-4 or set aside funds to cover the tax. Not a substitute for tax advice — consult your CPA if unsure.

benefits-bot: Automated notice: Benefits portal maintenance window: 2026-07-20 00:00 PT through 2026-07-24 23:59 PT. During this maintenance: new elections, investment changes, and in-plan transactions will be paused. Portal: https://benefits.redwood-inference.example/portal

alex: OK thanks. One more practical question — if I switch to Roth now, will the company match go into my Roth account or remain pre-tax?

anya: Good question. Our current plan design does NOT route employer matching contributions into employee Roth deferral accounts. Matches are credited to the traditional/pre-tax portion of the plan. We’ll update the portal FAQ with this to make it clearer.

marcus: Operational tip: if you want a deferral change to be effective for the 2026-08-15 payroll, submit by 2026-08-08. If you want to avoid any risk from the July migration, submit before 2026-07-15.

alex: Great — I’ll make the change in the portal today. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

anya: Awesome — ping @anya or email benefits@redwood.com if you hit any errors during submission :wave:
